topic: Vomit: Clean Up Claude's Verbose Token Output with a Separate LLM

key_points: Vomit converts Claude's token vomit into English by piping it through a local LLM; fully local, no telemetry, no external dependencies.
Hooks into Claude Code via the MessageDisplay hook, buffers Claude's output, forwards it to a local LLM, waits for a rewrite, then displays the fixed version in the session UI.
Recommended local models: GPT-OSS 20B via Llama.app; also works with Ollama, Apfel, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
Non-invasive 'tail' mode shows rewrites side-by-side instead of replacing Claude's display.
Disclaimers: the local LLM can only see Claude's message (no file/action access) so it can hallucinate; vibe-coded; slow; press ctrl-o in Claude Code to see the original output.
Install: go install github.com/zachahn/vomit@latest; then 'vomit init' and 'vomit scrub -claude'. GPL-3.0, 193 stars, 42 commits.
Author's launch post reasoning: it's wasteful to pay Anthropic per token then spend token budget on 'how to speak' instructions that Claude ignores or makes worse.
Claims OpenAI's free, small 20B open-source GPT-OSS model writes better than frontier Opus — a strong justification for the second-LLM cleanup approach.
Includes concrete before/after example showing a verbose Claude message (with caveats, verification lists, hedging) condensed into concise clear prose by Claude x Vomit GPT-OSS-20B.
Positioning: 'We are engineers, we build solutions, we are better than begging big arrays...'
HN thread on the Vomit launch captures the pain: users call Opus 5 output 'slop vomit' and find PR descriptions and comments copied from Claude unreadable.
Alternatives users share: a 'deslop' skill/gist that cleans Claude output; telling Claude to never write docs and delegating to a separate 'uvx swival --profile qwen' tool.
One user uses Haiku as a subagent with no context to reword long-task output, then the main agent fixes inaccuracies.
Skepticism: the editor model can hallucinate, omit details, or hide nuance — so test in non-invasive side-by-side mode first (also warned in the aipricing.guru review).
Some users found prompt/output-style tweaks ineffective and prefer the deterministic second-LLM rewrite.

Same 'clean LLM output with another LLM' pattern for structured data: primary LLM (Claude) does reasoning; a secondary cheaper LLM (Mistral 7B via Ollama, or GPT-3.5 Turbo) parses, validates, and reformats into strict JSON/YAML/markdown.
Measured 70-80% cheaper cleanup pass with Mistral vs a Claude re-parse prompt (~150-200 input+output tokens per cleanup vs ~50 in + ~20-30 out for Mistral).
Concrete 20% overall reduction in downstream token waste across a trade-recommendation workflow (100 iterations, 20% total), while adding only tens-to-low-hundreds ms latency.
Pattern generalizes beyond JSON to YAML and markdown tables; temperature ~0.01 for deterministic cleanup.
Pricing-impact analysis: Vomit is a workflow tool, not a Claude discount. It CANNOT recover or reduce Claude tokens already generated and billed.
Financial upside = avoiding a paid second rewrite turn + saving human reading time, NOT reversing the original output cost.
Local cleanup (own machine) adds zero hosted-API token charge but adds local compute and latency.
Risks: the local editor can hallucinate, run slowly, or omit important nuance; recommends side-by-side/tail mode before replacing Claude's displayed output.
Who benefits most: developers already running a local model (no extra metered API call; the editor doesn't need repo access since it only edits the message).

stats.fact: Verbose tool output (file reads, logs, search results) is over half of a typical Claude Code bill on Lineman's benchmarks.
On Lineman data, model routing: Sonnet costs about a fifth of Opus per token (15 vs 25 per million input/output, June 2026).
Context compounding: every turn re-sends the whole conversation as input, so bulky tool output read once is re-billed on every later turn — session cost grows with length.
A dedicated secondary-LLM cleanup pass cut downstream token costs by ~20% across a trade-recommendation agent workflow (measured over 100 iterations).
Mistral-7B-via-Ollama cleanup was 70-80% cheaper in token count than a Claude-based re-parse prompt: ~150-200 tokens vs ~50 in + ~20-30 out per cleanup pass.
Claude Sonnet 5 API rates tracked by aipricing.guru: $40/M in, $15/M input share, $25/M output share (Vomit cleanup adds no hosted token charge when run locally).
Vomit (GitHub) reached Hacker News on Aug 20, 2026; 193 stars, GPL-3.0, Go, no telemetry, no external dependencies.
Context-compression research shows up to 20x compression with small-model token pruning (LLMLingua) and 88-96% total token reduction in agentic workflows via entropy-based compression.

angles: Why Claude's verbose 'token vomit' is a real, costly problem — and why prompt-engineering fixes ('be more concise') fundamentally fail because Claude burns your paid tokens trying to speak differently.
The core insight: use the right tool for the job — a large reasoning model for understanding, a small cheap (often local) model for rewriting/formatting, separating reasoning from style.

Cost mechanics readers get wrong: a second-LLM cleanup does NOT cut Claude's original bill; it saves by avoiding a paid second rewrite turn, cutting reading/review time, and shrinking downstream re-parse tokens.
The pattern generalizes beyond Vomit: the same 'cleanup model' architecture works for JSON/YAML/markdown, PR descriptions, commit messages, and docs — a fundamental multi-LLM orchestration design.

Practical risk-aware setup: run cleanup model locally (zero hosted token charge), use non-invasive side-by-side/tail mode first, keep ctrl-o access to the original, and always let a human (or the main agent) validate fidelity against hallucination.
Open-source small-model irony: OpenAI's free GPT-OSS 20B beats frontier Opus at clarity — you may already own a better style model on your own laptop.
